definition: The number of people in a group or organization, which influences software pricing, feature requirements, and deployment considerations.
extendedDefinition: Team size is the number of people a software purchase supports, and it shapes pricing, feature needs, and deployment decisions. Small teams value simplicity, low entry cost, and fast setup, while larger organizations need administration, permissions, and rollout processes beyond the feature set itself. Pricing models interact strongly with team size: per-seat pricing punishes headcount growth, while tiered or flat pricing can reward it, so cost projections should follow realistic hiring plans. Feature requirements also shift, since collaboration, governance, and integrations matter more at scale. Deployment considerations include role-based access, provisioning and deprovisioning workflows, and training programs sized to the user base. Buyers should verify that the vendor's tier boundaries and administrative controls match the team today and its plausible growth, because product changes mid-contract are expensive. Matching capability to team size prevents both overbuying and premature scaling.
